_comment: Copy to company_config.json and edit. Everything below is read at startup by backend/config/loader.py — no orchestration code changes needed to onboard a company.

knowledge._comment_documents: Real, checked-in example content — see docs/handbook.pdf (generated by scripts/generate_example_docs.py) and docs/policies/*.md.
knowledge._comment_crawl_urls: docs/example_site/ is a static example support site, served locally so ingest.py's crawler has something safe to crawl without touching a real company's live website. Run: uv run python -m http.server 8080 --directory docs/example_site — then leave this list as-is (or point it at your own real support site's URLs once you have one).

mcp_servers._comment_internal: internal_tools is backend/mcp/internal_server.py — a real, runnable MCP server exposing rag_search/scrape_url/run_code plus stub lookup_order/check_policy. Start it with: uv run python -m backend.mcp.internal_server --port 9001. 'manager' is deliberately absent from tiers below — the Manager tier is local-tools-only by design (see backend/graph/tiers/manager.py), MCP starts at vice_president.
mcp_servers._comment_external: web_search is Tavily's real, hosted MCP server (https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp/) — no local process to spawn, no sandboxing needed, since it's a remote HTTP endpoint like 'crm' below. Needs a free Tavily API key (1,000 credits/month, no credit card — app.tavily.com/home) in TAVILY_API_KEY (see .env.example); the ${VAR} syntax pulls it from the host environment rather than storing the secret in this file. Tavily's MCP server also supports fully keyless, rate-limited access with no account at all: swap the headers entry for {'X-Tavily-Access-Mode': 'keyless'} and drop TAVILY_API_KEY entirely. (An earlier version of this example used Brave Search's stdio MCP server — Brave killed its free tier in February 2026, and every remaining plan needs a card on file, so Tavily is the documented default now.)
